observations: Multiple red cardboard boxes stacked and wrapped in clear plastic.
Brand name 'ARNOLD' with an eagle head logo is prominent on all boxes.
Text on the boxes reads '12V 100Ah' and 'Maintenance-free battery'.
Model number 'CMF 60038 DIN100' is visible on several boxes.
Text 'KOREAN TECHNOLOGY' and 'MADE IN P.R.C' (China) is printed on the packaging.
Certification marks for ISO 14001 and ISO 9001 are visible.
The items appear to be in a retail or warehouse setting.

claims.evidence: Text 'Maintenance-free battery' is printed on the box in photo 0.
100Ah is a high capacity for standard passenger cars, but performance is not proven by the box.
The DIN100 designation and 12V 100Ah specs are standard for automotive batteries.

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a different, used, or lower-spec battery.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual battery outside of the box showing the labels and terminals.
risks.if_unproven: as a used battery of unknown health

risks.risk: The battery may be old stock and have lost its ability to hold a full charge.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturing date code stamped into the plastic casing of the battery.

risks.risk: The battery may be defective or discharged below a recoverable level.
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading the resting voltage of the battery.

proof_requests: Photo of the battery out of the box showing the top and side labels.
Close-up photo of the manufacturing date code stamped on the battery casing.
Video of a voltage test using a multimeter.
response.reason: The brand, model, and specifications are clearly legible on the retail packaging, allowing for a valuation based on the worst-case scenario for a new-in-box unit of this specific brand.
